To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

motion sickness-related brain processes are located in the left and right motor, parietal, occipital and occipital mid-line areas, and that the spectral changes of these processes are associated with the degree of motion-sickness.
motion sickness-related brain processes can be identified using ICA and that the power changes in the brain processes are related to motion sickness.

1) motion sickness can be reliably and continuously induced using a VR-based simulator with six degrees of motion freedom; 2) five brain processes are consistently identified in all subjects, which exhibit different spectral changes in response to motion sickness; 3) the spectral changes in these brain processes can be used to evaluate the severity of motion sickness.

The main takeaway from our work is that
motion sickness-related brain dynamics can be disentangled from the brain dynamics induced by vestibular stimulations.
the brain dynamics of motion sickness are characterized by a combination of both power suppression in the alpha band and power augmentation in the theta and delta bands.

motion sickness can be characterized as a combination of brain responses that are associated with the vestibular system and visual perception, and that these responses may vary from subject to subject.
